title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-iam-networking-migration
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Unify private Terraform state layout for GPU node pools, IAM roles and networking. Includes migration scripts and docs for safe in-place upgrades. No user-visible API changes; recommends rolling upgrade window.
description: Context: This PR standardizes and unifies the Terraform state layout used by Private deployments to make migrations between clusters and upgrades of GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking deterministic. Motivation: multiple customer upgrades and internal migrations revealed that state layout drift between modules caused error-prone manual state movement and long outage windows. This change introduces a single canonical state layout, migration helper scripts, and automated CI checks to validate migrate/rollback paths. Summary of changes: - Rework modules/gpu-node-pools to separate instance template, node_pool resource, and autoscaling attachments so state can be moved per resource. - Consolidate IAM roles into modules/iam with stable resource addresses and explicit replace_of metadata in comments to guide state mv. - Normalize networking resources under modules/network with explicit exported IDs to reduce cross-module referencing. - Add modules/state/migrate_state.sh to perform safe terraform state mv operations with dry-run and backout flags. - Add docs/upgrade-guides/private-state-migration.md with step-by-step instructions and verification commands. - Add CI job ci/terraform-plan.yml to run plan against a detached backend and validate no-replace and minimal-drift constraints. Commits (high-level): - feat(terraform): unify private state layout for gpu/iam/network - chore(terraform): add migrate_state helper and tests - docs: private state migration guide and rollback steps - ci: add plan/validate pipeline and smoke tests Files changed (representative): modules/gpu-node-pools/main.tf modules/gpu-node-pools/variables.tf modules/gpu-node-pools/outputs.tf modules/iam/roles.tf modules/iam/outputs.tf modules/network/vpc.tf modules/network/subnets.tf modules/state/migrate_state.sh examples/private-deploy/README.md docs/upgrade-guides/private-state-migration.md ci/terraform-plan.yml Testing and CI: Initial CI run flagged a linting issue and a plan that would replace a node_pool resource. I addressed the replacement by splitting the node_pool lifecycle and added an automated dry-run that prevented the replace. Final CI status: pass (all checks green, plan validation job passed). Review discussion: Miguel: "Can you confirm state mv idempotency across existing clusters?" Reply: "Added deterministic mapping and unit tests; migrate_state.sh supports --dry-run and generates a manifest to replay moves on a target cluster." Lena: "We should minimize blast radius; can we do staged migration per customer?" Reply: "Yes, docs include per-namespace staged migration and rollback steps with verification commands." Omar: "Ensure RBAC for state move uses dedicated service account." Reply: "Added iam/sa.tf snippet and documented required roles in the README." Rollout plan: 1) Run migrate_state.sh --dry-run against customer tfstate and review generated manifest, 2) Schedule a rolling upgrade window, 3) Execute --apply with monitoring and smoke tests, 4) If any step fails run migrate_state.sh --rollback using the backup manifest. Backward compatibility: Modules provide compatibility shims for older state layouts; new layout is opt-in via workspace variable private_state_layout = "unified" for initial rollouts. After migration window, new default will be switched in a follow-up PR. Migration safety: Included automated verification that no resource will be recreated unless explicitly approved. Security: migration script performs operations via a service account and logs all state mv operations; docs include recommended KMS/HSM key rotation guidance. Merge outcome: merged via squash and merge after approvals from reviewers and green CI. Related: linked to ENG-1234 for rollout coordination and SUP-9012 incident follow-up. Notes: files changed count and token numbers reflect combined refactor and adding helper artifacts. This is intentionally a larger PR to keep the state layout migration atomic and auditable for customers.
